sentences.text: In Part Zero, we proved that zero plus n equals n.
We wrote the same claim in ACL2, with a hypothesis saying that n is a natural number.
Today, keep that one small example in view: the written claim, its proof, and what it means.
Those are three different things, and separating them explains the purpose of this project.
A proof can be checked by a computer, while questions remain about the rules that computer is checking.
We will build from our arithmetic example to models, consistency, and Gödel's second incompleteness theorem.
Then we can say precisely what is gained by moving an argument to a weaker foundation.
This is Part One of Landau Windows ACL Two: proofs, models, and stronger foundations.

chapter: What makes a proof step valid?

sentences.text: A formal proof is a finite sequence or tree of justified steps.
Some steps are starting axioms; others follow from earlier steps by a stated inference rule.
Here is one familiar rule: p holds, and p implies q, so q holds.
The letters here name claims with truth values, rather than natural-number inputs.
We can inspect the four possible pairs of truth values.
When p is true and q is false, the implication is false, so the two premises cannot both hold.
The only row in which both premises hold has q true as well.
That is why this inference preserves truth.
The ACL2 statement underneath expresses the same rule, and our teaching book checks it.
A larger proof links many such justified steps; its final line is the conclusion.
Checking one supplied proof asks whether its steps obey the rules.
Now give the written symbols an interpretation.
For ordinary arithmetic, zero names zero, successor adds one, and the variables range over natural numbers.
An interpretation that makes every axiom true is called a model of the theory.
To see why every axiom matters, try a different interpretation: a clock with three positions.
Its successor operation moves from zero to one, from one to two, and from two back to zero.
Before we call that clock operation by name, here is its full ACL2 definition.
Defun introduces video-clock-next, with the input n.
Nfix keeps n unchanged when it is natural, and returns zero for other objects.
We add one, then mod takes the remainder after division by three.
For input two, the intermediate total is three, and the remainder is zero.
Now fold the definition into its name, while keeping the inputs and outputs visible.
This call is video-clock-next at two, and its value is zero.
But PA requires that a successor never equals zero.
The ordinary natural-number successor satisfies that rule.
The clock fails it: the successor of two is zero.
This proposed clock interpretation already fails one of the PA successor axioms.
A few familiar equations can survive an interpretation while another axiom fails.
To claim that we have a model, we must justify all the axioms, including every instance of induction.
Consistency concerns the entire collection of possible formal proofs.
For PA, we can express it by saying that no valid PA proof ends with zero equals one.
A system that derives a claim and its negation is inconsistent.
In classical logic, contradictory premises allow any conclusion; the ACL2 formula illustrates that principle.
This is why consistency is a basic requirement for a useful foundation.
Checking this one arithmetic proof does not examine all other possible proofs.
Nor does checking a billion proof files establish that no longer contradiction proof exists.
We need a general argument about every permitted proof, however long it is.
One route to that argument uses a model.

chapter: How set theory supplies a number system

sentences.text: ZFC is a theory whose variables range over sets.
Its name abbreviates the Zermelo Fraenkel axioms together with the axiom of choice.
We will use one construction rather than list all of its axioms.
Start with the empty set and call it zero; it has no elements.
To build the next number, collect the elements already present and add the previous number itself.
One is the set containing zero; two is the set containing zero and one.
Continuing gives a set representation of every ordinary natural number.
ZFC can also form the infinite collection of these natural numbers, usually called omega.
Within set theory, that whole collection is an object we can study.
Addition and multiplication can be defined on it by their recursive rules.
Two other set operations will be useful: a union collects the elements of a family of sets.
A power set is the collection of all subsets of a given set; a two-element set has four subsets.
These are set-theoretic constructions; our ACL2 arithmetic examples retain their explicit natural-number domains.

chapter: Why a model gives a consistency proof

sentences.text: Inside ZFC, construct the natural numbers and prove that they satisfy the axioms of PA.
This includes a uniform justification of the induction scheme, rather than checking a finite sample of instances.
Now take any alleged PA proof and follow its steps in that model.
The axioms are true there, and the inference rules preserve truth.
Induction on the finite proof therefore shows that its conclusion is true in the model.
This connection between derivations and truth is called soundness.
Zero and one are distinct in the constructed number system, so a valid PA proof cannot conclude that they are equal.
That yields a ZFC proof of the consistency of PA.

chapter: How a proof becomes a number

sentences.text: There is another useful viewpoint: a proof file is a finite string of symbols.
Assign numeric codes to symbols and encode finite lists of those codes as natural numbers.
Here is a tiny example using decimal digits, just to make the mechanism visible.
Start with a leading one, then append the digits two, zero, and three.
The successive codes are twelve, one hundred twenty, and one thousand two hundred three.
Each append operation multiplies the previous code by ten and adds the new digit.
The leading marker keeps a zero in the data from being lost at the beginning.
Now let us define that encoder before using its function name.

chapter: Show the digit predicate and encoder definitions

sentences.text: The encoder processes a list of digits; let us first name the basic list operations.
Car selects the first item; cdr selects the remaining list.
Consp asks whether there is a list cell still to process.
Here is the complete definition of the digit-list predicate.
For a nonempty list, the first item must be natural and below ten, and the remaining list must pass the same test.
At the end of a proper list, the tail is nil, the empty list; other atomic tails are rejected.
We can now fold this definition into the name video-digit-listp.
Next, here is the actual recursive encoder.
It has two inputs: the remaining digits and the accumulated code.
If a digit remains, append the first item by multiplying the code by ten and adding that digit, then recurse on the rest.
When no list cell remains, return the accumulated code.
The complete definition can now fold into the compact name video-encode-digits.
The quote marks this list as data; the starting code is one.
Calling the defined function on two, zero, and three returns one thousand two hundred three.
For a digit list and a natural starting code, our checked ACL2 theorem proves that the output is natural.
A real encoding of formulas and proofs also needs a specified grammar and proof rules.
The definitions we have shown implement the toy encoder; a complete PA proof checker is a separate construction.
With a full encoding and checker in place, questions about proofs can be expressed as questions about numbers.

chapter: A statement about every proof code

sentences.text: We can now unpack the phrase PA is consistent in arithmetic language.
Let a proof predicate test whether a natural-number code describes a valid PA proof of the chosen conclusion.
For consistency, the chosen conclusion is the contradiction zero equals one.
The claim is: for every natural-number code p, that code does not describe a PA contradiction proof.
The notation Con of PA is a short name for this standard formal consistency statement.
To turn this into a concrete ACL2 statement, we would first need a full PA proof checker.
That full checker is not implemented in the teaching book; this is a specification of what it would have to decide.
We are displaying a specification, not a consistency theorem admitted in our teaching book.
Notice the jump in scope: the digit example computed one code, while consistency rules out every contradiction-proof code.
That universal claim is where Gödel's theorem enters.
Gödel's second incompleteness theorem applies to theories with enough arithmetic and an effective description of their axioms.
PA is one of the standard examples.
Effective means that the rules can be specified by algorithms, as they are for the theories discussed here.
Use the usual arithmetic encoding of formal proofs and the resulting consistency statement.
If such a theory is consistent, it cannot prove that standard statement of its own consistency.
We are stating the theorem here; its proof requires the formal machinery behind provability.
For PA, the forbidden self-proof would be a PA derivation of Con of PA.
For ZFC, the analogous limitation concerns a ZFC derivation of Con of ZFC.
This is a precise result with hypotheses, rather than a blanket slogan about every conceivable formal system.
It leaves room for a stronger theory to prove the consistency of a weaker one.
The ZFC argument about the natural-number model of PA is exactly that kind of result.

chapter: Stronger rules and a smaller dependency budget

sentences.text: Compare the two statements on screen: ZFC proves Con of PA, and ZFC proves Con of ZFC.
The model construction supplies the first statement.
If ZFC is consistent, Gödel's second theorem rules out the second statement, with its standard proof encoding.
A consistency argument must therefore say which background supplies its reasoning.
Likewise, a proof of an ordinary arithmetic claim comes with some set of dependencies.
The claim zero plus n equals n can be established without building the whole set-theoretic model first.
A successful reduction replaces a use of stronger resources with a derivation using weaker ones.
The mathematical conclusion stays the same, while the assumptions we rely on become smaller.
This is the sense in which a proof with fewer foundational assumptions is a stronger assurance.
Finding such a reduction is mathematical work; writing the statement in arithmetic is only the starting point.

chapter: One more use of the model idea

sentences.text: The model idea also explains why inaccessible cardinals enter discussions of foundations.
A cardinal measures the size of a set: equal sizes mean that the elements can be paired one for one.
Infinite sets also have cardinal sizes.
A strongly inaccessible cardinal, called kappa, is an uncountable size with two closure properties.
First, the power set of any set smaller than kappa is still smaller than kappa.
Second, a union of fewer than kappa sets, each smaller than kappa, is still smaller than kappa.
These conditions let us build a particularly well-behaved universe of sets.
Build sets in stages, taking power sets at successor stages and collecting earlier stages at limit stages.
The sets appearing before stage kappa form the collection written V kappa.
If kappa is strongly inaccessible, V kappa is a model of ZFC.
Consequently, ZFC with that extra existence assumption proves the consistency of ZFC.
If ZFC is consistent, it therefore cannot prove that such an inaccessible cardinal exists.
A standard set-theoretic treatment of Lean's universe hierarchy uses a sequence of suitable inaccessible sizes.
That describes a way to model the foundation; the dependencies of a particular theorem still need their own examination.

chapter: What this project is trying to reduce

sentences.text: Return to our actual goal: an arithmetic account of the windowed Landau argument.
We want the same intended conclusion, reached through explicit functions and checked theorems about their behavior.
For each component, we need a statement, a proof, and an interpretation connecting it to the mathematics.
An ACL2 theorem is a concrete artifact in ACL2's logic.
A claim about PA strength additionally needs the arithmetic interpretation of the fragment and principles used.
The programming language alone does not settle that foundational comparison.
Nor does the existence of one verified numerical example establish a general success theorem.
The later parts will keep the mathematical statement beside its ACL2 counterpart and state the input domains.
They will also distinguish a proved component from an outstanding interpretation or composition obligation.
That is how reducing assumptions becomes a precise, reviewable result.
We now have three separate questions: what follows from the rules, what the symbols mean, and what justifies the rules.
A model connects the first two, and a consistency proof names the background in which that connection is justified.
Gödel's theorem explains why the background matters.
The next part returns to calculations we can inspect directly.
We will represent fractions and intervals exactly, then prove that their bounds survive arithmetic operations.
For example, two thirds lies between one half and three quarters; ACL2 can express that comparison with exact rationals.
Those small guarantees will become the error budgets behind the later search and Landau arguments.
Same mathematical target, with the dependencies made explicit.
